extraction.name: PASTIS (Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme-Series)
extraction.description: PASTIS is the first open-access Satellite Image Time Series (SITS) dataset with panoptic annotations for agricultural parcel segmentation. It contains over 2 billion annotated pixels covering over 4000 km², designed for training and evaluating panoptic segmentation models on satellite image time series.
extraction.creator: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot, Loic Landrieu
extraction.publisher: LASTIG, Univ. Gustave Eiffel, ENSG, IGN
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The PASTIS dataset was created with panoptic annotations covering over 4000 km² with over 2 billion annotated pixels, using satellite image time series from the Sentinel constellation for agricultural parcel segmentation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multi-temporal satellite imagery from the Sentinel constellation, organized as time series with temporal, channel, and spatial dimensions (T×C×H×W)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is specific to agricultural parcel monitoring using satellite image time series, and varying cloud cover can make analysis arduous. The approach is tailored to yearly SITS where targets are static, limiting generalization to other temporal dynamics.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset supports crop mapping with major financial and environmental stakes, including fair allocation of agricultural subsidies (50 and 22 billion euros per year in Europe and the US) and ensuring best crop rotation practices are respected.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The PASTIS dataset is intended for training and evaluating panoptic segmentation models on satellite image time series, primarily for crop mapping and agricultural parcel monitoring. It can also support semantic segmentation tasks.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is open-access. A bug fix was applied to the panoptic metric computation after the original ICCV 2021 publication, with corrected results made available and tracked on GitHub.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Group Normalization with 4 groups is used instead of Batch Normalization in the encoder to address the issue that batches' samples are not identically distributed due to images acquired at different times.
